title: Three Former Presidents of the Mexican Republic in the National Conversation
author: Anahí Del Ángel
content:
_This article by[Anahí Del Ángel](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/anahida/)
originally appeared in the [October 2, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/tres-expresidentes-de-
la-republica-en-la-conversacion-nacional/), a Mexican investigative journalism
magazine._

_On September 30, former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador reappeared in a
video message to present his book Pueblo, and took the opportunity to
criticize neoliberalism and its main executors in Mexico, as well as to warn
that Fobaproa will not be fully paid off until 2055. That same day, the PAN
former presidents Felipe Calderón and Vicente Fox took part in the América
Libre Forum, where they vindicated their right-wing campaign; in response,
President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo defended the full force of freedoms in
Mexico, rejected Calderón’s claims of supposed links between Morena and drug
trafficking, and highlighted the political presence that AMLO maintains._

The public reappearance of former President **Andrés Manuel López Obrador** to
present his book **_Pueblo_** led President **Claudia Sheinbaum** to reflect
on the **“obsession”** that the media maintain with the former president, even
though he left the Presidency on September 30, 2024. She asserted that the
millions spent to discredit the leader of the **Fourth Transformation** do not
and will not have the expected effects on the population: “I am certain that
**López Obrador is in the heart of the people of Mexico and he will never
leave it** because he was a great leader and a great president; **50 years
dedicated to politics without failing the people, nobody forgets that**.”

In his message, López Obrador questioned the conventional media –radio, press
and television– which, he said, ran campaigns against him for years. He
defined them as **media of “manipulation”** at the service of **“the richest
men in the world”** and maintained that they are now moving their strategies
to the digital environment.

He stated that behind their journalists are the **“machuchones”** or
**economic potentates** , who use those platforms not only to inform, but also
to **blackmail the “corrupt politician”** and force him to **“submit and pay
for impunity.”**

As an example, he mentioned public spending on official advertising: **80
billion pesos** that, he said, the government of **Enrique Peña Nieto** handed
out. He added that during his term he reduced those resources, which, in his
view, provoked the anger of this sector.

For her part, Sheinbaum questioned that **Felipe Calderón** spoke about
**democracy** during his participation in the **América Libre** forum. She
recalled the irregularities denounced around the July 2, 2006 **presidential
election** , whose official result gave the victory to the PAN politician by a
margin of **0.56 percentage points** over López Obrador:

> Doesn’t it seem symptomatic to you, at least? I mean, you come to power
> through electoral fraud and then you talk about democracy.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

She also referred to the conditions for practicing journalism during
Calderón’s six-year term and asserted that there were agreements with media
owners to limit the dissemination of information: **“You devoted yourself,
among other things, to making pacts with the owners of the media to prevent
the truth from being told back then, and you talk about freedom of
expression.”**

Although the head of the federal Executive did not identify a specific pact,
in March 2011, 715 media outlets, among them **Televisa and TV Azteca** ,
signed the **Agreement for the News Coverage of Violence** , which established
criteria for reporting on **criminal violence**.

In that period, the use of **official advertising** as a mechanism of pressure
against critical media was also documented. In August 2010, the then United
Nations Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Opinion and Expression, **Frank La
Rue** , carried out a joint mission in Mexico with the **Special
Rapporteurship for Freedom of Expression of the Inter-American Commission on
Human Rights (IACHR)** , during which the conditions of violence and impunity
faced by the press were examined.

The report resulting from that visit was later presented to the **United
Nations Human Rights Council** and, based on figures from the National Human
Rights Commission (CNDH), recorded **the murders of 66 journalists between
2000 and December 2010 and the disappearances of another 12 between 2005 and
2010** , in a context of widespread impunity. The document also addressed the
**judicial harassment and the withdrawal of official advertising from media
for the independent exercise of their journalistic work**.

The President also rejected the PAN former president’s claims about a supposed
link between the **Morena** government and drug trafficking groups. During
Calderón’s administration, the Secretariat of Public Security was headed by
**Genaro García Luna** , against whom a **guilty verdict was issued on
February 21, 2023 by a jury in a federal court in New York** , for crimes
related to his collaboration with the **“Sinaloa Cartel”** and for false
statements.

The former official was found **guilty on five counts: four related to drug
trafficking and one for false statements**. On October 16, 2024, he was
sentenced to 38 years and four months in prison. In response to Calderón’s
accusations, Sheinbaum said: “It is truly unbelievable, I mean, how is he not
ashamed? Honestly, the bare minimum of shame.”

Referring to the forum that brought together representatives of the Mexican
and international right, the President considered that the opposition parties
are once again turning to the former presidents **“because they do not have
political cadres who can defend positions.”**

About Vicente Fox, she stated: “They have **Fox, traitor to democracy** ,
because during his term –and besides, we already know how he got there, with a
pact in the United States with **[Ernesto] Zedillo** – **he promoted the
desafuero and the electoral fraud**. And now he is the one going around the
country, and Calderón. I mean, **they are the ones running the campaign**. I
say, let them keep at it, honestly, go ahead, welcome.”

Sheinbaum linked these appearances to the building of an opposition alliance
heading into the 2027 elections and maintained that the former presidents have
resumed an **active role in the political discussion**. She noted that two
parties had ruled out forming an electoral coalition again, but that now
**“they are promoting the alliance of the two parties because if you look at
the polls, they are not doing very well, to put it mildly.”**

In contrast, she considered that López Obrador’s video shows that he retains
political presence, even though he no longer holds public office. On the
reactions to his intervention, she said: “**The hatred just pours out of their
pancreas** , they are going to get sick […] but it is an interesting moment.”

The President also responded to the words of her predecessor, who called her
“the best president in the world,” and described the message as **“very
emotional.”**

Finally, she rejected the protest carried out at **Los Pinos** during
Calderón’s visit, in which former workers of the defunct **Luz y Fuerza del
Centro** **decapitated the statue of the PAN politician**. The piece had been
lying on the ground for just over a year, after a tree knocked it down.
